unit.why: A short anecdote about R. Zusha choosing between two roads by seeing the divine Name, quoted from Divrei Moshe and set inside a homily on Lev. 9:6.
unit.boundary_note: The previous division is a related anecdote about R. Yitzhak of Drohobycz lost in a forest. The trailing 'מענין דרשה' is a catchword heading for the next section.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי שהה״ק אדמו״ר מוה׳ זושא זלה״ה הלך
stories.summary_en: R. Zusha, unsure which of two roads to take, saw the Name YHWH standing before him on one of them and took that road; the homilist uses this to teach that a deed is commanded if God's glory comes of it.

tags.why: The anecdote is wrapped in an exegesis of 'וזה הדבר אשר צוה ה׳' with a homiletic lesson.

quotes: לזאת מלמדו הכתוב כאן זה הדבר אשר צוה ה׳
tags.why: A verse interpretation is quoted from a homiletic book.

quotes: הלך פעם בדרך ולא ידע לאן יפנה
tags.why: The tsaddik's journey is the setting of the anecdote.

quotes: וראה באיזה דרך השם הויה עומד לנגדו
tags.why: He sees the divine Name in a waking vision.

quotes: וראה באיזה דרך השם הויה עומד לנגדו
tags.why: He perceives supernaturally which road is right.

quotes: השם הויה עומד לנגדו ובדרך זו הלך
tags.why: A divine disclosure guides his choice.

missing_concepts: divine guidance in decision-making / discerning God's will
